source_snapshot.procedure: Output dmidecode before and after, then compare Onboard Device Type and Description String.
source_snapshot.criteria: Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting.
source_snapshot.script: Private path ends in `type-41_onboard-device.git`, while the title, Procedure and DeepSeek command require SMBIOS Type 10. Five minutes attended and five machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES with `dmidecode -t 10`, but exposes a password, disables host-key checking, suppresses errors and greps only one line rather than every device entry.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; preserves Type 10, requires a type-10/type-41 owner decision, complete records and an approved reboot/recovery path.

old_problem: The Master title, Procedure, fields and generated command consistently request legacy SMBIOS Type 10, but the private Script URL names Type 41. The prior review treated the distinct schemas as requiring an engineering choice. DeepSeek also truncated a variable-length multi-entry Type 10 structure and could falsely pass empty/error output. The missing platform device oracle and reboot contract are Project inputs, not a reason to invent equivalence.
disposition_reason: DMTF resolves the schema relationship without a new universal engineering ruling: Type 10 is obsolete starting with SMBIOS 2.6 and Type 41 should be used instead, while BIOS providers may implement both for compatibility. Because this exact row's title, Procedure and command all name Type 10, its original branch captures every Type 10 entry and compares Device Type/enabled status/Description before and after one approved reboot. The private Type 41 script cannot silently satisfy that branch; it is retained as an optional separate modernization using Type 41's native fields. If—and only if—the exact platform SMBIOS/BIOS specification proves it intentionally implements Type 41 only and omits obsolete Type 10, the original Type 10 branch receives documented N/A and Type 41 evidence is reported separately. Missing expected inventory or applicability documents yield NOT READY, not Pending.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1448 was read through the repository extractor with row hash match, together with same-row tests.json, exact GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, duplicate search and the locked queue. The next formal identity was independently read as row 1455 / variant bf534cdad773bf2b.

DMTF SMBIOS DSP0134 v3.9.0 section 7.11 marks Type 10 obsolete starting with SMBIOS 2.6, directs implementations to Type 41, and explicitly permits BIOS providers to implement both for older browsers. Obsolete therefore does not mean forbidden or universally absent.

Type 10 is a variable list in which each device entry contains a combined Device Type/enabled-status byte plus Description string. Complete evidence must preserve the structure handle and every entry index; a header plus one grep line is incomplete.

Type 41 is not a byte-for-byte substitute: it represents one extended onboard-device instance and adds reference designation, instance, segment group, bus and device/function information. Its native records must be parsed separately before any project mapping to physical devices.

For this row, three independent Master surfaces—Items, During Test fields and DeepSeek's base `dmidecode -t 10`—select Type 10, while only a private and unreadable script path names Type 41. Case-specific precedence keeps Type 10 primary and does not establish a blanket rule that titles always win.

An authoritative platform conformance/BIOS specification can legitimately declare a Type-41-only implementation. That makes the obsolete Type 10 branch not applicable; an empty command alone, missing package or implementation defect cannot confer N/A.

Correctness requires an owner-approved board inventory mapping each expected onboard device to Type 10 enum, enabled bit and exact/normalized Description. SMBIOS metadata proves firmware inventory, not electrical presence, link, driver or functional operation.

The before/after criterion requires one controlled warm OS reboot, same-target Boot ID transition and OS Ready recovery. The read commands themselves are non-mutating, but the reboot remains service-impacting, explicitly approved and never retried automatically.
Source log clearing is rejected: preserve the pre-reboot baseline, reboot interval and post-state so absence, parse errors and firmware/boot regressions remain auditable.

ED-03/ED-04/ED-22 permit Project inventory/applicability bindings; ED-13/ED-14 retain reboot authorization and safety; ED-15 requires authoritative N/A; ED-26/ED-29 require first-outcome and full boot-state evidence; ED-33/ED-35 preserve original Type 10 coverage; ED-36 makes expected values readiness; ED-38 reserves the verdict.

test_case.test_name: SMBIOS Type 10 all-entry correctness and reboot persistence, with separate Type 41 applicability
test_case.purpose: Verify every implemented SMBIOS Type 10 onboard-device entry's device type, enabled status and Description against the exact board specification and across one approved warm reboot, while treating the source's Type 41 script as separate modernization and permitting Type 10 N/A only from authoritative platform implementation evidence.
required_package: Exact host/BMC/board/revision, BIOS version/build and reported SMBIOS major/minor version; versioned platform BIOS/SMBIOS conformance or implementation statement
Owner-approved onboard-device oracle listing each physical/logical device identifier, expected Type 10 Device Type enum, enabled state, exact or normalized Description and duplicate/missing policy

Validated `dmidecode` package/version with least-privilege read access to SMBIOS, secure authenticated transport if remote, parser that preserves complete raw output, DMI handle and every device-entry index

If Type 10 is claimed N/A: explicit target documentation that obsolete Type 10 is intentionally not implemented and Type 41 is the supported inventory; if Type 41 is collected: separate Type 41 expected fields and physical-device mapping
Approved maintenance window and exact warm-reboot command, console/BMC/OOB recovery, stable power, target correlation, baseline log retention and protected evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY COLLECTION AROUND ONE APPROVED REBOOT; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind Source Key/variant and capture exact host/board/BIOS/SMBIOS identity, Boot ID, BMC/OS health and preserved logs. Record `dmidecode --version`; execute privileged `dmidecode --type 10` without grep or stderr suppression, saving command, status, stderr and complete raw structures. Parse every Type 10 structure into `(handle, entry_index, device_type_enum, enabled_bit, description)` and compare the semantic device inventory with the approved board oracle. If no Type 10 structure exists, do not PASS: require the target's versioned Type-41-only implementation authority for N/A, otherwise report NOT READY/FAIL. Optionally invoke the retained private Type 41 script only after package inspection/hash/approval, or use `dmidecode --type 41`; save Type 41 in a separate dataset with reference designation, device type/status, instance and PCI coordinates—never merge it into Type 10 results. After explicit reboot approval and recovery confirmation, issue the exact approved warm reboot once, correlate Boot ID and same target through shutdown/startup to OS Ready, then repeat the complete Type 10 collection/parser/spec comparison and any separately approved Type 41 collection. Diff semantic entries and preserve raw output/logs; make no BIOS, device, driver or firmware change.
test_case.expected_result: When the platform specifies Type 10, every expected entry is present exactly once with the correct standard device type, enabled bit and Description before the reboot and remains semantically identical and specification-correct after the same target reaches OS Ready; commands complete without hidden errors. When authoritative target documentation specifies Type-41-only behavior, Type 10 absence is recorded as N/A with that citation and separately collected Type 41 evidence matches its own oracle. No metadata result is represented as proof of device function.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS for the Type 10 branch requires target/SMBIOS identity, complete successful raw collection, every structure/entry parsed, exact owner oracle, correct type/enabled/Description for all entries, one approved Boot ID-changing warm reboot, OS Ready and identical correct post-state with no unexplained log/health regression. FAIL covers a present/required Type 10 entry that is missing, extra, duplicated contrary to policy, disabled/wrong type, incorrectly described, malformed, changed after reboot, or accompanied by boot/health failure. NOT READY covers missing oracle, access/parser, reboot approval or recovery. Type 10 N/A requires explicit platform implementation authority—not empty output, obsolete status alone or a Type 41 script name. Type 41 may PASS only its separately labeled modernization and never cross-credit original Type 10 coverage.
safety_gate: SMBIOS collection is read-only. Do not change onboard-device enablement, BIOS settings, drivers, bindings, firmware or physical hardware, and do not infer functional health from metadata.
Use authenticated host access and least privilege; never expose passwords, disable host-key/certificate validation, suppress stderr or accept empty/truncated output.
Preserve complete raw structures and logs. Do not clear dmesg, system logs or SEL before the reboot; distinguish command failure, no structure and authoritative non-applicability.

Require explicit maintenance approval immediately before the warm reboot and verify BMC/console recovery. Do not substitute cold/AC/DC cycling and do not automatically retry reboot or collection after failure.
Do not run the private Type 41 script merely from its URL. Inspect provenance/hash/content and approve it first; otherwise use a supported read-only Type 41 reader for separately labeled evidence.
Never map Type 41 to Type 10 by similar descriptions alone. Require a versioned per-device Project mapping, and keep native schema fields, raw output and coverage results distinct.
The review agent executes no reboot, command, script or DUT test and issues no hardware PASS.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, host/BMC/board/revision, BIOS build, SMBIOS version, dmidecode/parser versions and target implementation/conformance document
Owner Type 10 inventory oracle with device identity, enum/enabled/Description expectations and normalization/duplicate rules
Complete pre/post `dmidecode --type 10` stdout/stderr/status, structure handles, all entry indexes, parsed tables, semantic/spec diffs and cryptographic evidence hashes
Reboot approval, exact command, old/new Boot IDs, same-target BMC/console timeline, OS Ready and preserved OS/BMC/SEL health evidence
For Type 10 N/A, explicit platform Type-41-only citation; for modernization, separately labeled complete Type 41 native records, approved script/tool identity and device mapping
No setting/device/driver/firmware/log mutation, no retry and no-DUT-action-by-review-agent statement; Tool Result separate from engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Before reboot, verify the console/BMC path and preserve the complete correct pre-state. If the reboot fails to reach OS Ready, use only the approved boot recovery runbook, retain the first Boot ID/timeline/logs and do not automatically reboot again. If Type 10 records disappear, drift or fail parsing, do not change BIOS/device state or run Type 41 as a substitute; capture complete SMBIOS tables and firmware identity, keep the system in a diagnosable state and escalate to the BIOS/platform owner. If the private script is unavailable or untrusted, omit only that modernization step and retain original Type 10 evidence.

source_conflict.reason: DMTF defines the precise relationship and the row itself consistently selects Type 10. The Type 41 URL is retained as a distinct modernization path, not an equivalent core method; a documented Type-41-only platform receives explicit Type 10 N/A rather than silent substitution.

blocked.reason: The command semantics, schema distinction, acceptance and recovery are defined from the standard. Expected device entries, implementation applicability, package and reboot window are bounded Project inputs that gate readiness.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact board/BIOS/SMBIOS identity; Type 10 expected device enum/enabled/Description inventory; Type-10 implementation or authoritative Type-41-only/N/A statement; parser/tool and optional private-script approval; reboot command/window; OOB recovery and post-boot health policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER READ-ONLY/REBOOT DEFINITION ONLY; NO DMIDECODE, PRIVATE SCRIPT, REBOOT, BIOS, DEVICE, LOG, DUT OR OTHER HARDWARE ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: DMTF SMBIOS Specification DSP0134 v3.9.0
external_authorities.application: Section 7.11 defines Type 10 as obsolete since SMBIOS 2.6, recommends Type 41 and permits both; the Type 10 and Type 41 native record models determine the separate parsers and evidence.

project_authority: The BIOS/platform owner supplies the implemented-schema declaration, Type 10 inventory oracle and any per-device Type 10/41 relationship; operations approves one warm reboot and recovery. They may document Type 10 N/A for an authoritative Type-41-only target, but cannot use obsolescence or empty output alone, silently substitute Type 41, waive original Type 10 coverage on a platform that implements it, or treat metadata as functional validation.
